haiku-low.q1: MySQL commits first, then the same request applies the row to Postgres under the copy rule with a 500 ms timeout. A Postgres failure or timeout never changes the response; the row stays queued for the sweeper.
haiku-low.q2: Only when no tombstone exists for the id and the stored version is lower than the incoming version. A missing row is inserted.
haiku-low.q3: Every instance must report users_dual_write=on, held for 60 s, before users_backfill is turned on. Flags have a 30 s cache, so instances can disagree for about 30 s.
haiku-low.q4: The backfill reads the MySQL replica in batches of 2000 rows. It waits while mysql_replica_lag_seconds exceeds 5, polling once per second.
haiku-low.q5: Before reads move: a clean 3.1 pass within 24 h and no forward-queue row older than 5 min. Before the source moves: 72 h at 100% reads, a zero-mismatch 3.1 pass, an empty forward queue, replica lag under 5 s, and dual write on everywhere.
haiku-low.q6: The users_sync_queue row in MySQL, written in the same transaction as the write. The sweeper retries with exponential backoff until the copy succeeds and the queue row is removed.
haiku-low.q7: Each delete writes a tombstone in the same transaction. Every copy takes a per-id lock and does nothing if a tombstone exists.
haiku-low.q8: Progress is backfill_last_id in migration_state, written in the same Postgres transaction as the copies. It stops when a batch returns no rows (backfill_status=done) or when a persistent conflict raises an alert.
haiku-low.q9: The 3.1 comparison pass finds differing id ranges and confirms mismatches after a recheck. Confirmed mismatches go to the forward queue: MySQL-held rows are copied to Postgres, Postgres-only ids are tombstoned and deleted.
haiku-low.q10: Users_source=paused stops user writes, and every instance must show paused within 30 s with in-flight writes at 0. If the switch runs long, restart stragglers and record pauses over 90 s; never set mysql again.
haiku-low.q11: Postgres assigns ids from its sequence, set to max(id) across both databases plus 1,000,000 before the switch. After rollback, MySQL AUTO_INCREMENT gets the same max plus 1,000,000 offset, avoiding collisions.
haiku-low.q12: A reverse queue and reverse sweeper copy Postgres writes to MySQL, checked by 3.2. Rollback pauses writes, drains the reverse queue, sets MySQL AUTO_INCREMENT, then sets users_source=mysql. The option ends at 7.2 (pg_only).

sonnet.q1: MySQL first: in one MySQL transaction the users row change plus a forward-queue row (and tombstone for delete) is committed. Then, after commit, the same request applies the row to Postgres (500 ms timeout, request waits at most 500 ms). If the Postgres part fails or times out, the user's response is unchanged (normal response); the queue row stays for the sweeper.
sonnet.q2: Only if no tombstone exists for the id and the stored Postgres version is lower than the incoming version (INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE ... WHERE users.version < EXCLUDED.version). Done under the per-id advisory lock. Equal or older versions never overwrite.
sonnet.q3: Before backfill (2.1): users_dual_write=on on every instance (every instance reporting app_flag_value=on, and that gate held for 60 s). Instances can disagree up to about 30 s after a flag change (the flag cache refresh); a 60 s wait covers it with margin.
sonnet.q4: Backfill reads from the MySQL replica, not the primary; batches of 2,000 rows; before each batch it waits while mysql_replica_lag_seconds > 5, polling once per second. (Only that is stated; no other throttle is described.)
sonnet.q5: Before reads move (4.1): a clean 3.1 comparison pass within the last 24 h and no forward-queue row older than 5 min. Before the source moves (Phase 5.1): 4.2 complete (72 h hold at 100% reads with zero mismatch), latest 3.1 pass has zero mismatches, forward queue empty, mysql_replica_lag_seconds < 5, every instance reports users_dual_write=on.
sonnet.q6: The forward-queue row (users_sync_queue, with user_id and queued_at), written in the same MySQL transaction as the change, in MySQL (primary), records it. The repair sweeper (a worker holding a lease in migration_state) reads queue rows, applies the copy rule from the current MySQL row (or tombstone and delete if the row is absent), then compare-and-deletes the queue row.
sonnet.q7: Tombstones (user_tombstones in each database), written in the same transaction as any removal. Every copy runs under a per-id lock and, if a tombstone exists, does nothing. Deletes write the tombstone before deleting the row.
sonnet.q8: In migration_state in Postgres (backfill_last_id; absent means 0). The cursor is updated in the same Postgres transaction as the batch's row copies, so they cannot disagree. The backfill stops when a batch returns no rows, then sets backfill_status = done.
sonnet.q9: The comparison job (3.1), started by hand on a worker: walks both tables in id ranges of 2,000, comparing row count and a hash of (id, version, email, name, plan, updated_at); re-reads mismatched ids from both primaries, rechecking after 2 s if rows changed. Each confirmed mismatch goes into the forward queue and the sweeper repairs it (copy MySQL row to Postgres, or for Postgres-only ids write the Postgres tombstone and delete the row). A pass with mismatches doesn't count; the next must be clean.
sonnet.q10: A pause: users_source=paused makes writes return a retryable 503 (Retry-After: 2) while reads continue; gate that every instance shows paused within 30 s and in-flight writes reach 0 within 5 s; queue drained within 10 s; then set pg and every instance must show pg within 30 s. Pause must stay within 90 s (budget at most 75 s). If it runs long before 5.4: set users_source=mysql and stop/abort (in-flight over 10 s, drain over 10 s, not all paused in 30 s). After 5.4 it cannot be aborted: restart instances still showing paused, record a pause over 90 s as a violation, do not set back to mysql; roll back via Phase 6.
sonnet.q11: Postgres, via a sequence. To avoid collisions, the sequence is set to max(id) across both databases plus 1,000,000 (MySQL max read from the primary) during the pause. After rollback, MySQL AUTO_INCREMENT is likewise set to max(id) across both databases plus 1,000,000 (6.2).
sonnet.q12: While source is pg, each write commits to Postgres with a reverse-queue row, then is applied to MySQL under the copy rule (500 ms timeout), with a reverse sweeper repairing; 3.2 reverse comparisons (start of 5.5, daily, before 7.1). Rollback (Phase 6): pause writes, drain the reverse queue to zero (10 s cap), set MySQL AUTO_INCREMENT to max+1,000,000, set users_source=mysql. Available from 5.4 until 7.2; after users_source=pg_only (7.2) reverse copies stop and rollback is no longer possible.
